Subject: Purchase process & legal routing for Redwood evaluation

Alex — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of outcomes from discovery:
- Primary use case: 3-month pre-prod pilot to replace legacy embedding/semantic search for customer support (approx 5M input tokens/month during pilot).
- Decision criteria: inference latency at P95 < 300ms, unit token cost < $0.0008 after batching, successful security review (keys + audit logs).
- Timeline aim from Finex: pilot kickoff early July, production decision by end of Q3.

Stakeholder map (please confirm owners):
- Economic buyer: Priya Singh (we heard you say CFO).
- Procurement owner: TBD (we expect procurement@finexcorp.com).
- Legal owner (contracts/Data Protection): TBD.

Recommended legal routing and sequencing (our take):
1) NDA (mutual, non-prod data-safe) — quick DocuSign, target turnaround: 2 business days.
2) MSA (commercial + SOW) — start with a commercial-only signature to enable pilot; full MSA redlines to follow. Target turnaround: 7 business days after receipt of redlines.
3) DPA (data processing addendum) — run in parallel with MSA review if legal wants to prioritize, typical turnaround 3–5 business days.

Reasoning: small, phased sign path minimizes blocking for the pilot while preserving leverage to finalize privacy terms before production. If procurement insists on MSA first, we can flip sequencing but expect longer lead times.

Attachments: redwood_requirements_matrix.xlsx (an intake we fill), redwood_msa_v1_redlines.pdf (our standard starting point).

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm the legal/procurement contacts and preferred turnaround times?
- Can we get a firm name for the economic buyer so I can loop them into a short 20-minute call next week?
- If you agree with the sequencing above, we will: 1) send NDA today via DocuSign, 2) prepare a commercial-only MSA for quick signature, and 3) schedule a MAP review with the procurement/legal owners.

Proposed slot for MAP + econ buyer intro: Tue Jun 7 or Wed Jun 8, 10–11am PT.

Thanks — I’ll hold on sending anything until I have the contacts and a quick confirmation of turn times.

—

Team — quick internal notes on routing and risk posture before we send anything externally: 

1) NDA: we should send a short mutual NDA via DocuSign and offer a 2 business day SLA. Keep the NDA language minimal (purpose, confidentiality, term). We can sign and get the ball rolling.

2) MSA strategy: propose a two-step MSA approach for speed —
   - Step A: commercial-only MSA (terms: pricing band, pilot scope, termination, liability caps at pilot scale) signed quickly to allow pilot provisioning.
   - Step B: full MSA with detailed SOW and indemnities + DPA to follow during or right after pilot.

3) DPA: offer our standard DPA template; legal can work in parallel with MSA. If Finex legal insists on much heavier redlines up front, escalate to Rishi to coordinate.

4) Redline sequencing & turn times (recommended internal SLAs):
   - NDA: 2 business days (DocuSign).
   - MSA commercial-only: 48–72 hours turnaround for straightforward commercial changes.
   - Full MSA + DPA: 7–10 business days depending on redline depth; escalate if >10 days.

5) Pricing confirmation: before sending MSA for signature we need final confirmation of expected committed capacity (even a soft band works). Dylan — please confirm the expected token volume and the pilot spend band you discussed.

Attachments: redwood_msa_quicksign_summary.pdf (internal summary of what we send for a commercial-only MSA).

If we align on the above, I recommend we send NDA via DocuSign today, prepare commercial MSA draft, and request procurement intake form fields be returned within 48 hours to keep things moving.
